title: Join D-REP
heading:
At the Data Representation Lab (D-REP), we investigate how representations shape the ways people perceive, understand, and interact with information. This positioning presents itself as a creative opportunity to innovate the future while addressing current limitations (i.e., flat 2D desktop visualizations).

Our innovations and “out-of-the-box” thinking enable us to situate data into mediums and contexts that have never been considered (e.g., dome-scale visualizations; 3D-printed network visualizations). Through this stance, we present new data representation paradigms that are unique to our technical strengths.

subheading.title: OPEN POSITIONS AND OPPORTUNITIES
subheading.text: We welcome curious, motivated individuals who are excited about bridging technology, science, and human experience. We embrace diverse perspectives, experiences, and backgrounds. Our lab thrives at the intersection of machine learning/AI, human-computer interaction, data visualization, and computational design. Whether you are a graduate student, postdoc, undergrad, or visiting researcher, there. Whether you are a graduate student, postdoc, undergrad, or visiting researcher, there are many ways to get involved. Below is an overview of open roles, expected qualifications, and how to apply.

why.title: Why Join Us
reasons: Work on cutting-edge problems at the convergence of ML/AI, mixed reality, physical interaction, and cognition
Collaborate across disciplines—computational design, engineering, science, psychology
Gain experience in prototyping, user studies, fabrication, design, and visualization
Opportunities to publish and present in top-tier venues in HCI, visualization, AR/VR, cognitive science, and beyond
Be part of an interdisciplinary team of deep thinkers and brilliant makers

content.text:
We are seeking 1–2 Ph.D. students for the Fall 2027 incoming class through the University of Arizona's Department of Computer Science. D-REP is co-directed by Profs. Sandra Bae and Takanori Fujiwara, whose research spans human-computer interaction, data visualization, computational methods, and interactive physical systems.

We welcome students with strong technical foundations, intellectual curiosity, and an interest in interdisciplinary research. In addition to applying through the official application portal, prospective students are encouraged to contact the D-REP co-directors with the materials listed below.

listing.title: Research Focus: Prof. Sandra Bae — Human Perception, Cognition, and Learning
listing.text: Prof. Bae is particularly interested in recruiting a Ph.D. student at the intersection of cognitive science, human perception, and computer science. A central question motivating her research is how the design of external representations shapes what people perceive, learn, remember, and reason about. She seeks students interested in combining computational approaches with rigorous behavioral experiments to understand how people acquire and use knowledge from different representations.
items: Human perception, cognition, and learning: investigating how visual, spatial, interactive, and physical representations influence understanding, memory, and reasoning
Computational modeling of human cognition: developing and testing models of how people learn and build internal representations of complex information, including networks and relational structures
Behavioral experimentation: designing controlled experiments to investigate the cognitive effects of different representations and identify underlying mechanisms
Representation design: using insights from cognitive models and empirical studies to develop principles for designing more effective data representations

content.text: Applicants interested in Prof. Bae's research are especially encouraged to apply if they have experience or interests in cognitive science, computational modeling, experimental psychology, HCI, or visualization. Skills in programming, experimental design, statistical analysis, or computational modeling are valuable, but expertise in all these areas is not required. We value rigorous thinking, research curiosity, and a willingness to learn across disciplines.

listing.title: Additional Research Directions at D-REP
listing.text: Beyond the research focus described above, D-REP welcomes prospective Ph.D. students interested in the broader research directions pursued by Profs. Bae and Fujiwara, including:
items: Machine learning and AI technologies for visualization and physicalization (e.g., dimensionality reduction)
3D large-scale visualizations for network and high-dimensional data
AR/VR applications for data-driven discovery and analysis in STEM domains (e.g., optics, materials science)
Interactive computing applications to improve engagement and learning in AI and data science
Computational design pipelines using machine learning and data-driven optimization to fabricate interactive 3D-printed data objects and network physicalizations
Empirical studies investigating the perceptual effectiveness of data physicalizations

listing.title: Broader Research Opportunities
listing.text: We also welcome students interested in exploring one or more of the following directions:
items: Leveraging mathematics and computation to advance the fundamental science and understanding of interactive data representations
Using computational fabrication and geometry to expand the functionality of data physicalizations, including sensing, output modalities, mechanical behavior, and actuation
Developing and refining reinforcement learning methods to generate, explore, and optimize 3D-printed physicalizations
Developing hardware and computational design tools for interactive data representations

listing.title: What to Include When You Apply
listing.text: Prospective students should apply through the University of Arizona Computer Science Ph.D. program. You are also encouraged to contact the D-REP co-directors (Sandra Bae and Takanori Fujiwara) with the materials below. Please indicate whether you are primarily interested in working with Prof. Bae, Prof. Fujiwara, or both, and briefly explain how your interests align with their research. If you have external fellowship funding or plan to apply for fellowships, please mention this in your email.
items: CV or résumé
Portfolio or representative work (e.g., research projects, prototypes, publications, or demos)

Research statement describing: (1) your research interests and motivations, (2) relevant skills and technical expertise, (3) why you are interested in working with D-REP and your preferred faculty advisor, and (4) potential research questions or project directions you would like to explore

content.text: We welcome research associates, visiting scholars, and interns (undergraduate or graduate) from diverse backgrounds, both domestically and internationally. Projects can be short- or mid-term, and may be paid or volunteer depending on funding and role.

listing.title: Expectations & Duration
items: Commitment of at least 6 months is preferred (for productivity and training)
Prior experience in programming, prototyping, or user studies is a plus
Working closely with lab members across domains

content.text: Please contact the D-REP co-directors (Profs. Bae and Fujiwara) to apply.

We welcome both University of Arizona undergraduates and undergraduates from other universities, who are interested in gaining research experience in the areas of machine learning, visualization, digital fabrication, user-centered research inquiry, and experimental characterization. We discourage one-semester-only involvement, as many components of our research (computational design, fabrication, user studies, prototyping) require onboarding.
Students interested in long-term (one year or more) intensive research projects are encouraged to contact the D-REP co-directors (Profs. Bae and Fujiwara).

Undergraduates may participate in research voluntarily in the lab. However, to seek funding or course credits, UArizona undergraduates can check out here for funding opportunities. Including, Vertically Integrated Projects, Course-Based Research Undergraduate Experiences (CUREs) for course cre dits, Summer Research Institute (SRI) and College of Science Research Scholarship for funded opportunities.

For undergraduates outside of UArizona, you may seek funding opportunities from your home school.
